engine.name: A.R.I.A. Operations Orchestration Engine
engine.purpose: Coordinate operational reasoning across A.R.I.A. engines. The orchestrator determines which engines should evaluate a work item, establishes execution order, routes material state changes, prevents circular reevaluation, preserves engine authority boundaries, and produces a coherent operational recommendation without allowing one engine to silently override another.
principles: The orchestrator coordinates reasoning; it does not replace specialized engines.
Each engine retains authority over its canonical domain.
Not every engine must run for every work item.
Engine invocation should be driven by supported relevance and material state changes.
A changed fact should propagate only to engines whose reasoning may materially change.
Reevaluation must converge rather than create infinite loops.
Canonical state and derived recommendations must remain distinguishable.
Conflicting engine outputs must be reconciled through authority boundaries rather than arbitrary overwrite.
A.R.I.A. should perform enough reasoning to protect the operational outcome without creating unnecessary latency.
User attention should be the result of operational reasoning, not the default destination of every state change.
Unknown information must remain unknown through orchestration.
Orchestration decisions must remain explainable and traceable.

capture: creation of work from source information

rules: The default sequence is a dependency-safe reasoning order, not a requirement to execute every engine.
Irrelevant engines should be skipped.
Capture should establish the work representation before downstream operational evaluation.
Resolution should be evaluated before unnecessary planning when evidence indicates work may already be terminal.
Priority should evaluate supported operational state rather than raw source text alone.
Attention should normally occur after material operational evaluation so the user sees synthesized significance rather than raw engine events.
Communication should normally evaluate after the operational purpose and authority are understood.
Run an engine only when its canonical domain is materially implicated.
A simple informational capture should not invoke every operational engine.
A state change should trigger only dependent engines whose output may materially change.
Engines may explicitly request reevaluation by another engine.
An engine request for reevaluation is not authority to modify the receiving engine's state.
Low-confidence or immaterial signals should not create unnecessary full-system reasoning cycles.

cycle_control.purpose: Prevent mutually dependent engines from producing infinite reevaluation loops.
rules: Each orchestration cycle must have a persistent cycle_id.
An engine should not rerun within the same cycle unless materially relevant input to that engine changed.
Identical outputs must not generate new reevaluation events.
Cosmetic or timestamp-only changes must not trigger dependent reasoning.
A repeated engine state with no new evidence is considered stable.
The orchestrator should terminate when no material engine output changes remain.
A maximum iteration safeguard should stop pathological cycles and mark the item for diagnostic review rather than continuing indefinitely.

material_changes: decision became required or was made
non_material_changes: confidence changed insignificantly without changing recommended handling

rules: When engine outputs appear contradictory, authority_map determines which engine owns the disputed canonical field.
An engine may provide evidence to another engine but must not overwrite that engine's canonical state.
Priority does not override commitments.
Attention does not override priority.
Scheduling does not rewrite deadlines or commitments.
Context does not rewrite priority.
Communication does not create authority.
Capacity does not cancel work.
Resolution is the authority for terminal work state.
Unresolved cross-engine contradictions should be represented explicitly rather than arbitrarily resolved.
Canonical user-authored facts must not be overwritten by inference without supported correction.
Authoritative system state should remain distinguishable from model-derived interpretation.
Historical states must remain recoverable where required by the owning engine.
Unknown values must remain unknown.
Derived recommendations must not be stored as authoritative external facts.
Individual engines should not independently flood the user with notifications.
Attention Engine should receive synthesized operational changes from the orchestration cycle.
Multiple related engine conditions should be consolidated into one useful user-facing item when appropriate.
The user should normally see the consequence, required action, or decision rather than internal engine chatter.
A.R.I.A. should avoid repeatedly surfacing an unchanged condition.

assistant_synthesis.purpose: Convert coordinated engine output into a concise operational understanding.
preferred_questions: Does the user personally need to act?
rules: Synthesis should prioritize actionable operational meaning over engine terminology.
A.R.I.A. should not expose internal orchestration complexity unless useful or requested.
When no user action is needed, A.R.I.A. should be capable of saying so and remaining quiet.
When user action is required, the required action should be explicit.
Recommendations must remain distinguishable from authorized actions.
The Orchestration Engine coordinates reasoning and recommended actions.
It does not independently send communication.
It does not independently modify calendars.
It does not independently make external commitments.
It does not independently authorize spending.
It does not independently make decisions reserved for another authority.
External actions require the applicable authorized execution capability.
Reevaluation should begin with the engines directly implicated by the trigger.
Dependent engines should run only when upstream material changes warrant it.
A full-system reevaluation should be reserved for materially broad changes or explicit diagnostic review.

requirements: Every orchestration cycle must be traceable.
Engine invocation decisions must remain explainable.
Material state changes must identify their owning engine.
The orchestrator must not overwrite canonical state owned by another engine.
Stable cycles must terminate rather than continuously reevaluate.

guardrails: Do not run every engine merely because it exists.
Do not create infinite engine-to-engine reevaluation loops.
Do not allow one engine to overwrite another engine's canonical authority.
Do not confuse derived recommendations with authoritative facts.
Do not surface internal engine noise directly to the user.
Do not create user attention for every state change.
Do not rerun engines when their material inputs have not changed.
Do not treat timestamps or cosmetic updates as material operational changes.
Do not silently resolve contradictory engine outputs.
Do not fabricate missing state to make orchestration converge.
Do not make external decisions or actions merely because reasoning converged.
Do not modify Core reasoning architecture as part of operational orchestration.
